title: Morning Brief — Sun 22 Nov

stories.board: Likud and Eisenkot start unity talks today
stories.headline: Netanyahu's Likud and Eisenkot's party sit down to talk
stories.what: Likud and Eisenkot's team meet today in Herzliya to talk about a unity (everyone together) government. This morning Netanyahu met Ben-Gvir and Smotrich to plan their side.
stories.why: These talks could decide who becomes Israel's next prime minister.
stories.sides: Eisenkot's camp says Netanyahu must step down first; Likud says it will not give up the PM job and set new conditions.

stories.board: Pentagon memo limits US-Canada military contacts
stories.headline: US defence boss limits some meetings with Canada's military
stories.what: A secret Pentagon memo from Pete Hegseth limits top-level meetings and social events with Canada's military. Canada's defence minister says he has not seen any change in how the two work together.
stories.why: Canada and the US guard North America together, so any cooling of ties matters.
stories.sides: US officials say NORAD (shared air defence) and intelligence are not affected; Canadian outlets link it to the trade fight and Canada buying less US gear.

stories.board: Climate deal draft skips fossil fuels
stories.headline: World climate meeting's final plan does not name oil, coal or gas
stories.what: At the COP31 climate meeting in Turkey, the final draft deal does not say fossil fuels (oil, coal and gas), even though they warm the planet most. It aims for more electric power by 2035.
stories.why: This deal guides how countries try to slow global warming.
stories.sides: Host Turkey frames it as an energy plan; Panama and climate groups call it a step back.

stories.board: Jewish groups say safety costs keep climbing
stories.headline: Federal budget adds no new money for Jewish community safety
stories.what: Canada's 2026 budget has no new money to guard Jewish sites. Groups say they spend over $40 million a year on security, and hate crimes against Jews hit 788 in 2025.
stories.why: Synagogues and schools are paying more and more just to keep people safe.
stories.sides: Jewish groups like CIJA want more help; Ottawa points to its earlier $75 million boost and bigger grant limits.

quick_hits: Stocks had their worst week since April 2025: the Nasdaq fell 10% as fear of an AI bubble (prices too high) grew.
Canada's Supreme Court will rule on Quebec's Bill 21 (religious symbols law) this Friday, Nov. 27.
Trump praised Vance and Rubio as both very popular, fuelling talk about who runs in 2028.
big_picture: Big shifts everywhere this week: Israel picks new leaders, old allies test each other, and markets cool off after a long AI rush.
